# Erdős #242: Erdős–Straus three unit fractions

[All problems](../README.md) · [Lab](../../README.md) · [Progress](../../PROGRESS.md) · [Contribute](../../CONTRIBUTING.md)

**Project focus: ACTIVE.** Study exact obstructions to bounded first-denominator templates for 4/n as three unit fractions.

## The question

For every integer n>2, do positive integers x<y<z exist with 4/n=1/x+1/y+1/z? This lane checks scoped denominator formulas, not counterexamples to the conjecture.

## Read this first

A failed first-denominator formula is not an Erdős–Straus counterexample. Character obstructions here are necessary conditions, with literature priority unchecked; no global theorem is claimed.

### Character obstruction to two first-denominator shifts

Prime p=2521≡1 mod840 defeats both x=(p+3)/4 and x=(p+7)/4, but admits an exact triple with a different x. This is a restricted ansatz counterexample only.

Formalization: **UNFORMALIZED**. Literature: **PRIORITY_UNCHECKED**.
Evidence baseline: `b7d02f5ff6ec8b5e898610af5c47adc95928627d`. No CI execution is claimed for this entry. Inspect the proof and its assumptions.

</details>

## Next bounded question

Can both shifts c=3 and c=7 be proved to fail for infinitely many primes p≡1 (mod 840), after comparing with Dahan's 2026 work?

**Discriminating test:** A candidate infinite prime family fails if one required member has a successful c=3 or c=7 template; finite samples do not prove infinitude.
